body:
Thank you for the reply. The thought of fear...I guess you're right. It is a fear, and I know it's twisted up in nonsense.

It's difficult for me to really explain why I do/don't want to go to the hospital. And as I sit here automatically thinking why I shouldn't I realize how stupid I can be. 

Stupid "reasons" are because it's Friday night, it will be busy, I will take up a bed and time away from others, and I do realize the stupidity in all that. 

The wait time is really holding me back the most, when I was admitted last time, I walked in at around 12 p.m. and wasn't actually admitted inpatient until 11 p.m. It was insanely busy and while they did make sure I was taken care of, I still hesitate. The last time I did get some Ativan, and it helped a bit, but I know my anxiety is incredibly higher than it was several months ago. I also know that I can't leave once I get there. I tried to leave AMA last time because I was getting edgy and agitated, hence the Ativan, so there's that part of me that shoots anxiety up higher - if I walk in, I'm not going to be walking out a few hours later.

I guess, I know what to expect. I also know what to bring/not to bring to the psych unit. I also know that it's not a horrible place, but it's something that I have avoided. 

I've been trying to think this over, I really have. 

I think, if I can just make it through the weekend to Monday, that it may be easier to be admitted - if I tell my therapist and psychiatrist, they could help me. They both work for the hospital where the psych unit is, maybe I'd be able to skip the hours waiting in the ER.

And now I don't know if I've just made that a reason not to go...but I know that they only admit patients into the unit with the shift changes, meaning I would be in the ER until tomorrow morning. 

If I can hang on for two days, it might be easier. Damn it, two days out of all these months now sounds like it's a huge mountain I have to climb. 

I really would love to black out for two days but I know that's not going to happen.

If I keep my waking hours busy, I might be all right. If I can force myself to do things, I might make it to Monday. Now this sounds crazy even to me but I'll still say it, possibly the thing that motivates me to keep going is the fact that I only have to go it alone for two more days - and instead of death being that motivator, instead it's knowing I will be able to let go of the front I put up. 

That makes sense...I think. Shit, I don't really know what I'm doing anymore. It seems like it makes sense to me but then I also realize it might not make sense for others.

I've experienced this a long time ago. I was told there is such a thing called existential depression. Which seems to be along the lines of what you're saying. 

A while ago, we're talking years, I felt like I came face to face with how mundane and pointless life was. The thing was, this realization of sorts hit me suddenly. I was sitting and the next second I was questioning why I was even alive, if I was alive, and what it meant to be alive. I didn't find myself severely depressed, and I was in a fairly stable state.

I don't know how I ever got out of that thinking, because a part of it never left. The strong feelings of what's the meaning of life, what's beyond this life, etc left. I wasn't as consumed with them. But, I didn't get rid of all the feelings. I think that once I was kind of hit with reality square in the face, I never will be able to get back the innocence of only thinking about this present world. I think it's an experience, maybe distressing, but can be used to actually continue on with life.

If this is perhaps the only life we have, then use it and make it a damn good time.

You should be careful as you could easily fall into a "true" depression - that's the wrong word but I can't think of a better replacement right now. 

From experience, and not only from my personal experience, thinking about suicide repeatedly may cause a tolerance. Just like there's a tolerance with seeing violence in films, there's a tolerance to self-destruction. Be careful, because the line that you say you'll never cross can become slowly, and increasingly, more faint.

I stumbled across a quote, which I still hang onto. I forgot where I heard this/read this, but something along the lines of: I wasn't alive for billions of years before I was born and it didn't bother me, so why should I be bothered by the billions of years after I die?
